entries.note: PMID 12649388; quote verbatim in abstract; print Apr 2003. Untested correct. Model label adds Th2 cells, which Sugimoto did not test (eosinophils only); cosmetic.

PMID 22496329; quote verbatim; epub 2012-04-10, print Jan 2013 (41:46). Patient sputum eosinophils fell and ex-vivo PGD2 shape change was inhibited, matching the cell model. Paper itself measures the model readout in patients, so comparison_stated could be true.

PMID 22106101; quote verbatim; epub 2011-11-21, print Feb 2012. Untested holds: Bateman 2017 chose 150 mg by empirical FEV1 dose-ranging (primary met, p=0.0035), no occupancy comparison published. Singh 2013 ex-vivo -33.6% is a rule question.

PMID 17328802; quote verbatim; 2007. Untested holds. 'OVA' not stated in abstract ('mouse asthma model'). Clinical compounds never used this model (Schmidt 2013 verbatim: rodent cells unresponsive); class-proxy status belongs in the model field.

PMID 21762224; quote verbatim; epub 2011-07-15, print Jan 2012. Primary FEV1 missed and sputum eosinophils (the mouse readout) P=0.37 vs placebo; only secondaries hit. Not a match under rule 4. Hold untested; alternatives Singh 2013 LAR or Bateman 2017.

PMID 23174659; quote verbatim; epub 2012-11-20, print Feb 2013. AMG 853 antagonises PTGDR2, so in-class; contra at 2013 stands. If dual antagonists are excluded, contra moves to 2016 (Kuna 2016 AZD1981, Erpenbeck 2016 fevipiprant, both missed primaries), not 2021.

PMID 22106101; quote verbatim. Untested holds. Caveat 'never filed': ramatroban is marketed in Japan for allergic rhinitis (Sugimoto abstract) as a TP antagonist; no selective CRTH2 antagonist was filed for asthma (Novartis dropped its 2020 NDA plan). Maspero 2021 not re-verified.

fact_fields: efficacy 2 (Barnes 2012): source_calls_it should be 'match' (authors: 'first clinical evidence that CRTH2 receptors contribute to airflow limitation, symptoms and eosinophilic airway inflammation'), not null.

efficacy 3 (Busse 2013): source_calls_it should be 'miss' ('was not effective at improving asthma symptoms or lung function'), not null. product_in_model=false not verified (no AMG 853 mouse data checked).
engagement 2 (Singh 2013): comparison_stated=false is arguable; the trial itself measured the in-vitro model readout (PGD2 eosinophil shape change) ex vivo in dosed patients (-33.6%, n=7).

all cells: model_filed=false confirmed for asthma. Fevipiprant: Novartis planned a 2020 NDA gated on LUSTER, then said the results 'do not support further development' (biopharmadive.com/news/novartis-fevipiprant-asthma-phase-3-zeal-study-failures/565569/; pharmaphorum.com/news/novartis-axes-asthma-drug-fevipiprant-after-more-trial-woes/). Ramatroban (Baynas) is marketed in Japan for allergic rhinitis, approved as a TP antagonist before its CRTH2 activity was reported (Sugimoto 2003 abstract); not this context.
missing: Kuna 2016, two phase 2 RCTs of AZD1981 (selective CRTH2), primary morning PEF nonsignificant in both (P=0.086, P=0.16): https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S105142. Earliest selective-antagonist efficacy miss; decides the contra date if dual antagonists are excluded.

Erpenbeck 2016, fevipiprant 500 mg phase 2, n=170, no significant difference vs placebo in trough FEV1 or ACQ in the total population: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pupt.2016.06.005. Same role as Kuna 2016.

Bateman 2017, fevipiprant dose-ranging n=1058, primary pre-dose FEV1 met (p=0.0035, max 0.112 L): https://doi.org/10.1183/13993003.00670-2017. The cleanest efficacy 'same' for a selective antagonist; the draft cites it only in the dose judgement.

Singh 2013 (already cited for engagement) also reports a 25.4% reduction in the late asthmatic response (p=0.018) after allergen challenge, the closest patient analog of the allergen-challenge mouse; a defensible efficacy 'same' at 2013 if challenge studies count, in place of Barnes 2012.

LUSTER-1/2 (Brightling 2021, print vol 9 issue 1, epub 2020-09-24) should appear as its own efficacy entry (contra, 2021, engagement-proven, 1,771 patients) rather than only inside the 2013 judgement, since it is the comparison that settles the class.
rule_questions: Missed primary endpoint with nominally significant secondaries (Barnes 2012): is that 'same', 'contra', or neither? The brief does not say. The draft scores Barnes (missed primary, secondaries hit) as same and Busse (missed primary, nothing hit) as contra; a consistent rule is needed. Suggest: the primary endpoint or the source's own conclusion decides; secondaries alone leave the cell untested.

Does a dual DP1/CRTH2 antagonist (AMG 853) count as 'a drug of this class' for a PTGDR2-antagonist context? Literal reading: yes (it antagonises PTGDR2; DP1 blockade was itself expected to help, so it does not excuse the model) -> contra 2013. Selective-only reading -> contra 2016 (Kuna/Erpenbeck), never 2021.

Does a patient allergen-challenge study (Singh 2013: late asthmatic response, post-allergen sputum eosinophils) count as an efficacy comparison, or only as engagement? It is the direct patient analog of the OVA mouse.

Does an ex-vivo PD readout in dosed patients (Singh 2013: PGD2 shape change -33.6% at 200 mg bid, n=7, versus near-complete inhibition in vitro) constitute a dose comparison against the whole-blood pKB model? The draft says too thin; the brief does not decide.

Model attribution for efficacy: the clinical compounds were characterised in human cells and rat/guinea-pig PGD2-agonist eosinophilia models (Pettipher 2012), never in the OVA mouse (Schmidt 2013: rodent cells unresponsive). Is a tool-compound disease model acceptable as 'the model the class relied on'?
